questions.answer_text: Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor; it accepts electrons and protons to form water, allowing aerobic electron flow to continue.
questions.explanation: Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor. It accepts electrons and protons to form water, and this final acceptance allows electron flow through the aerobic chain to continue normally.

questions.answer_text: Fermentation keeps glycolysis running by regenerating NAD+, uses no oxygen as a terminal electron acceptor, and yields much less ATP than aerobic respiration.
questions.explanation: Fermentation does not replace glycolysis; it keeps glycolysis running by regenerating NAD+. It uses no oxygen as a terminal electron acceptor and produces much less ATP per glucose than aerobic respiration.
